acute-angle: An angle that measures more than $0^\circ$ and less than $90^\circ$.
angle: Two rays with the same endpoint. The endpoint is the vertex. Write $\angle ABC$, with the vertex in the middle.
collinear: Points that lie on the same line.
coplanar: Points or lines that lie in the same plane.
degree: The unit for measuring angles, written $^\circ$. A full turn is $360^\circ$. A right angle is $90^\circ$.
endpoint: A point at the end of a segment or the start of a ray.
intersect: To cross or meet. Two lines intersect at a point. Two planes intersect in a line.
line: A straight path of points that goes on forever in both directions. Write $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ or name it with one small letter, like line $\ell$.
measure-of-an-angle: How far an angle opens, in degrees. Write $m\angle ABC = 40^\circ$. Read it as “the measure of angle $ABC$ is 40 degrees.”
obtuse-angle: An angle that measures more than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$.
opposite-rays: Two rays with the same endpoint that go in opposite directions. Together they make a line.
plane: A flat surface that goes on forever in every direction. Name it with one capital letter, like plane $P$, or with three points in it that are not on one line.
point: An exact location. A point has no size. Name it with a capital letter, like point $A$.
ray: Part of a line that starts at one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. Write $\overrightarrow{AB}$: it starts at $A$ and goes through $B$.
right-angle: An angle that measures exactly $90^\circ$. A small square at the vertex marks a right angle.
segment: Part of a line between two endpoints. Write $\overline{AB}$. Its length is written $AB$, with no bar.
straight-angle: An angle that measures exactly $180^\circ$. Its sides are opposite rays, so it looks like a line.
vertex: The point where the two sides of an angle meet. The plural is vertices.
